messages.author: 5297b14c628baebd
messages.subject: Specifying groups in multi-session data
parts:
Hi,

I was hoping to get some sage advice on the best way to set up groups across multi-session data.  I have a restored/unrestored group and 4 habitat groups (5 sampling days for each of 7 sampling events).  Using prior advice, I broke each unique combination (e.g., CypressRestoredE1, CypressUnrestoredE1) into a session, but am having trouble grouping across sessions if I just want to estimate, for example, restored vs. unrestored across all habitat types.  Is this not an appropriate use of the multi-session format?  I have tried trap covariates ("Hab", "Res") but get the error that covariate levels are different across sessions. So the question is...once you break out sessions is it possible to do analyses that look across them?  What might be an alternative approach?  I've attached 2 of the 56 sessions from the study.

ch_sub<-read.capthist('capt_cypress1_2sess.txt',c('CyRe1.txt','CyUn1.txt'), trapcovnames = c("Hab", "Res", "Mo"), detector = 'count', fmt = 'trapID')


Thanks,

James

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Specifying groups in multi-session data
parts: "once you break out sessions is it possible to do analyses that look across them?"

Have you checked out session covariates? Provide a dataframe of covariates (one row per session) as the sessioncov argument of 'secr.fit' and you can use the column names in a model for multi-session data.
Murray

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: Specifying groups in multi-session data
parts: The error message is generated by the optional 'verify' step; set verify = FALSE in secr.fit to suppress this. It may be that the message relates to covariates that you do not use in a particular model (it won't be generated by non-factor numerical covariates).
